top_signals.title: Oil Prices Drop 7% as Iran, Qatar Open to Peace Talks
top_signals.summary: Oil prices fell more than 7% on Monday as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials lifted hopes for an end to the US-Israeli war with Iran and stabilization of Middle East crude supply.Iran's president said the supreme leader had granted the government "certain authorities" regarding peace talks.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Mideast Oil Prices Weaken as Crude Keeps Flowing Through Hormuz
top_signals.summary: Middle East oil market metrics are indicating near-term supply is outpacing demand for the first time since July, when global prices plummeted after a temporary ceasefire between the US and Iran allowed tankers to exit the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz.

top_signals.title: What Israel’s Election Results Mean for the Middle East and Beyond
top_signals.summary:
Israeli elections on Oct. 27 produced a complex result, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition alliance, led by Gadi Eisenkot, winning enough seats in the Knesset to form a government. The opposition faces a tricky choice: attempt to form a unity government with Netanyahu, after channeling anger at the prime minister during the campaign, or partner with the Israeli-Arab parties, which performed unusually well in the election. The latter option, however, is deeply unpalatable to most of the Jewish opposition. A period of negotiations now commences, while Netanyahu remains in a caretaker position. If no governing
